title: Donut Benchmark — Label Positioning

complexity.rationale: Split out of donut-benchmark at the user's request. The 'always lower-left, top-hanging baseline' anchor rule is genuinely Benchmark-specific (no other donut feature produces a fixed-position, non-hemisphere-mirrored label), but it reuses donut-direct-labels' width-based anchor-offset technique and its shared text-width approximation helper rather than inventing new measurement logic. What keeps this above a 2: the two label formats (single-line vs. two-line) and their fallback rule aren't fully specified, and the extra ~8px safety buffer is an unsourced practical adjustment that needs verifying against real rendering, not just transcribing a formula.

summary: The Benchmark line's label - always positioned at the lower-left of the line's outer endpoint - is not yet built. Confirmed via two live Figma examples showing both a two-line format (name + value, e.g. 'Last week' / '54.2%') and a single-line format (just a category name in bold, e.g. 'Target'). Depends on donut-benchmark for the line's outer-endpoint position (the anchor point this label is positioned relative to) and reuses donut-direct-labels' width-based anchor-offset technique and text-measurement helper.
requirements: Benchmark label supports two formats, both confirmed in the reference: a two-line format (a name line in `text-secondary`/gray-700, e.g. 'Last week', plus a value line in `text-primary`/gray-800, e.g. '54.2%') and a single-line format (just a category name in bold `text-primary`, e.g. 'Target').

Benchmark label position is always at the lower-left of the line's outer endpoint, left-aligned, using the same anchor-offset technique as donut-direct-labels (both lines start-from-the-near-edge/left-aligned to each other; the shared anchor's x = the line's outer-endpoint x minus the rendered block width, not a fixed pixel offset) - reuse donut-direct-labels' text-width approximation helper for the width estimate rather than reimplementing it.

Unlike donut-direct-labels' hemisphere-mirrored anchor (which flips left/right depending on which side of the ring a segment is on), this label's position is always lower-left regardless of the benchmark line's angle - a fixed rule, not a mirrored one.

Use a top/hanging vertical baseline (not centered) so the block reads below the endpoint rather than straddling it, plus an additional ~8px safety buffer (not a sourced token, a practical rendering safeguard) subtracted/added on top of the width estimate so the label clears the caret.
